title: Green's own degree: Bubbles' steps done several ways
summary: Green says his degree was versatility, Bubbles took them there to train, he joined at seventeen, and the club became his workshop.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, what was it that you brought to the Hoover's Club? What was your degree?

My degree was I had a kind of versatility. I could do the Buck and Bubbles tap dance steps. I could do them several different ways, the same step, see? But I had a great lot of freedom because I had a partner, and we eventually were taken down there -- Mr. Bubbles used to take us down there. He was the senior member of the Buck and Bubbles team. He used to take us down there to train us, you know, make us practice, take us through the paces, as he called it. He wanted to liven us up to keep our energies, you know, at a certain partiality, I'd say. See? And we were growing, you see, and that would make us straighten up and so on, like that.
Well, so how old were you when you first became a member of the Hoover's Club?
Well, I was getting to my 18th year. I was 17, actually, but I was kind of large, you know, for my age.
Now, Bubbles was also a member of the Hoover's Club.
Oh, yeah. A senior, you see. He had been

on the throne. See, that's really what made me wander down on this tour, there. It really became like a workshop for me, you know, because I knew that eventually we would be working with Buck and Bubbles again, you know, so I just got away with it, because I was trying to -- I caused a lot of joy there amongst the tap dancers. I made them kind of have more respect for each other's art, see.
